definition: A frame divided by two horizontal and two vertical lines into thirds creates four "power point" crosses that draw the eye more than the geometric center; placing a subject (or a horizon line) on one of these third-lines/crosses is the default composition, EXCEPT that dead-center framing is its own deliberate exception, specifically reserved for conveying authority or a teaching/informing role (a subject speaking directly to camera with intent to instruct).
purpose: Give subject placement a legible default (off-center, on a power point) while reserving the one clear deviation from it (dead center) for a specific, recognizable communicative purpose rather than treating center-framing as merely a failure to apply the rule.
visible_effect: A subject or horizon sitting on a third-line/power-point reads as more dynamic and intentionally composed than one sitting at the frame's literal center; conversely, a subject placed dead-center reads as authoritative or didactic specifically because it is recognizable as a deliberate departure from the more common off-center placement.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Off-center placement on a power point is described as conveying more emotion/emphasis than dead-center; dead-center framing is named as specifically signaling authority or a teaching role — the same source demonstrates this on itself, framing its own direct-to-camera instructional shots dead-center throughout.
physical_interpretation: Not applicable — a compositional/perceptual convention, not a physical principle.
use_cases: placing a subject or a horizon line on a rule-of-thirds line/power-point as the default composition for portraits, b-roll, and establishing shots
deliberately breaking the rule with dead-center framing specifically when a subject's authority, expertise, or didactic role is what the shot needs to communicate
non_use_cases: dead-center framing used out of inattention rather than intent — the exception's legibility depends on it being a deliberate, recognizable departure, not a default
interactions: static_camera_as_deliberate_emotional_withholding (W09-87) — a structural sibling: both entries are about a compositional/camera DEFAULT having a specific, opposite-reading DELIBERATE EXCEPTION (stillness withholding sympathy; center-framing asserting authority) rather than the exception being merely a failure to follow the rule

looking_room_ties_gaze_direction_to_frame_side_balance (this same video) — both are rule-of-thirds-derived compositional conventions; that entry adds the further constraint of matching frame-side space to gaze direction

style_variations.power_point_placement: the default: subject or horizon on a third-line/cross, read as more dynamic/emotionally engaging
style_variations.center_frame_authority: the exception: subject dead-center, read as authoritative or instructional

cadence_representation: Not measurable in this build at all: rule-of-thirds placement is inherently a SCREEN-SPACE fact (where does a subject project to within the visible frame), which requires an active camera with a projection model — exactly the capability named as absent throughout this batch's camera-related entries (MOT-006, SHOT-002/004, REV-001's blocked camera-framing analysis step, KNW-007's unmeasured "camera support" quality). Cadence's `ai/pose.js`/`ai/motion.js` measure world-space facts (line of action, centre of mass, joint rotation) that exist independent of any camera; this rule is defined ENTIRELY in terms of the camera's own view and cannot be evaluated from world-space data alone, however complete.
control_surface: None — no active-camera projection exists to place a subject against a rule-of-thirds grid.
detection_and_measurement_methods: not measurable in this build — requires projecting a subject's screen position through an active camera, which does not exist (the same MOT-006/SHOT-002 gap as this batch's other camera-framing entries).
failure_modes: defaulting to dead-center framing without the specific authority/teaching intent, losing the exception's meaning by making it the unremarkable norm
placing a subject off-center inconsistently (sometimes left third, sometimes right, with no narrative reason), reading as accidental rather than composed
roblox_considerations: None specific — applies to any rendered camera view, live-action or virtual.
examples: "the center of the frame is reserved for authority or for teaching... you'll notice in videos like this one right now the teacher is often center-framed looking right at the camera" (video @ 02:30–02:42), confirmed directly in this session's own frame reads — the presenter's own talking-head shots throughout are consistently dead-center

the rule-of-thirds grid overlay demonstrated directly on a park-bench establishing shot, an animated hot-air-balloon shot with the balloon on a power-point cross, a sunset with the sun on the lower-right third-line, and a close-up on a distressed character's face with eyes on the top third-line, all confirmed in this session's own frame reads (video @ 00:33–02:10)
